text:
Alex: Heads up — after the kernel-selector change in v2.4.2 I'm seeing a perf regression on multi-GPU TP runs. Latency spikes for long sequences when flash-attn is enabled. Timeline shows repeated QKV all-gather followed by idle and then big all-reduce backoffs.

Maria: Can you paste the short trace and the exact run cmd? want to see timing and whether kvcache sharding aligns.

Alex: repro command (internal bench):
```
./bench/tp_flash_profile --model t5-XXL --gpus 8 --bs 1 --seq 4096 --enable-flash --tp 2 --chunk-size 64
```
nvprof-ish summary (trimmed):
```
0.00s compute: fused_attn_kernel A
0.12s all_gather(QKV) rank0->rank1 48ms
0.16s idle wait 80ms
0.24s all_reduce 72ms
(repeats every layer, skew grows with seq length)
```

Jamal: hmm. Two thoughts: 1) kernel-selector recently started preferring a tiled QKV layout for certain seqlen distributions — that can change the all-gather pattern from a single large op to many smaller ops (more overhead). 2) kvcache sharding may be misaligned across TP partitions, causing extra memcpy/fallback into slower copy path in fused-attn.

Nate: I repro locally w/ 8xA100. nvprof shows many small ncclAllGather calls instead of fewer batched calls. Example from my trace: 
```
# layer 18
ncclAllGather size=262144 took 0.051s
ncclAllGather size=32768 took 0.013s
ncclAllReduce size=65536 took 0.078s
```
Overhead on the order of 10-30% just from extra collectives + scheduling gaps.

Maria: Did the selector change also flip a fallback for sequences that hit alignment != 64 bytes? If fused-attn sees misaligned QKV slices we sometimes call a non-flash fallback that forces extra host staging.

Alex: Yes - selector commit 8f3b9 changed the quantization/kerneltable threshold and added an "unified-tile" path. That path seems to split QKV differently.

Sophie: Quick mitigation: you can force the previous kernel via runtime flag: `--kernels=fused_qkv_legacy` and enable comm/compute overlap: `REDWOOD_ENABLE_COMM_OVERLAP=1`. That reduces wall time on my runs to ~+4% vs +22% with the new selector. Also pin model-serving to v2.4.1 for now.

Jamal: Long-term fixes to consider: 1) make kernel selector cost-model include NCCL op count + expected fragmentation; 2) canonicalize kvcache shard boundaries so QKV slices line up with TP partitions; 3) add a micro-batcher that merges small all-gathers into a single nccl call when topology allows.

Alex: I'll attach traces and open a perf/regression ticket with the selector diff and nvprof logs. Also trying a small patch to realign shard offsets to TP tile boundaries — early tests look promising.

Nate: For reproability, run with `NCCL_DEBUG=INFO NCCL_ALGO=TREE` and `REDWOOD_KERNEL_DEBUG=1` so we can see which kernel variant was chosen per layer.

perf-bot: [perf-bot] Created issue PERF-1729: "TP QKV all-gather fragmentation after kernel-selector change (v2.4.2)" and attached CI traces.

Maria: Good. let's schedule a short sync tomorrow with runtime + tp owners. Bring the nvprof + perf-map and the kvcache alignment patch diff.

Alex: Thanks — will add links in the ticket. initial hypothesis: selector splitting QKV into many small fragments + kvcache misalign -> flash-attn falling back or incurring many small collectives.

Sophie: If someone needs a quick patch for canary, I can push a flag to force legacy QKV layout for canary clusters.

Alex: That would help. tagging @SRE and @infra-ops in the ticket.

Nate: FYI I also saw a rare edge where sequence lengths divisible by 96 triggered a different scatter pattern — might be an off-by-chunk bug in the tiled layout generator. filing a small PR next.

Alex: Great — thanks everyone. I'll post updates in the PERF ticket and link the canary once Sophie has the flag up.
